classification.difficultyReason: Express the intersection point along two different lines, introduce a scalar for QO, and compare independent vector coefficients to determine k.

content.prompt:
The triangle $PQR$ is shown. $M$ is the midpoint of $QR$.

$\overrightarrow{PR}=\underset{\sim}{x},\quad \overrightarrow{PQ}=\underset{\sim}{y}$.

$\overrightarrow{PO}:\overrightarrow{OM}=3:2$.

$\overrightarrow{PN}$ can be written in the form $k\underset{\sim}{x}$.

Work out the value of $k$.

spec.description: Outline triangle PQR with horizontal PR, Q above, midpoint M on QR, N on PR, and segments PM and QN intersecting at O. All six labels are retained. No arrowheads, midpoint ticks or numerical dimensions.
spec.mathematics: M=(Q+R)/2; O=P+(3/5)(M-P); N is the intersection of QO with PR. Coordinates implement these relationships without printing additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry is supplied in the question; no solution annotations or scalar value are shown.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PR}&=\underset{\sim}{x},\quad \overrightarrow{PQ}=\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{QR}&=\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{QM}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PM}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QM}\\\overrightarrow{PM}&=\underset{\sim}{y}+\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\overrightarrow{PM}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

Since $PO:OM=3:2$,

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PO}&=\frac35\left[\frac12(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\right]\\\overrightarrow{PO}&=\frac3{10}(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})\end{aligned}$

Since $Q,O,N$ are collinear, write $\overrightarrow{QO}=m\overrightarrow{QN}$.

$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PO}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QO}\\\overrightarrow{PO}&=\overrightarrow{PQ}+m\overrightarrow{QN}\\\frac3{10}(\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})&=\underset{\sim}{y}+m(k\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\frac3{10}\underset{\sim}{x}+\frac3{10}\underset{\sim}{y}&=mk\underset{\sim}{x}+(1-m)\underset{\sim}{y}\end{aligned}$

Comparing coefficients:

$\begin{aligned}mk&=\frac3{10}\\1-m&=\frac3{10}\\m&=\frac7{10}\\k&=\frac37\end{aligned}$
